title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page writes down a presentation by generators and relations of a groupoid G~ that lies over a 'base' groupoid G attached to combinatorial data. The base data look like an oriented map (carte) described by flags.

Indexing data:
- Flags r = (s,a,ω) ∈ R, with s ∈ S (vertex-type data), a ∈ A (edges) and ω a face or rotation datum.
- Bijections R ≃ A×ω ≃ S×ω are assumed, so a flag can be indexed either by (a,ω) or by (s,ω).
- Operators σ0 and σ1 act on R (cartographic-group style): r' = σ0 r = (s,a'), and r1 = σ1σ0(r') = ω'r'.
- There is a cyclic operator ω on flags; the products d_{ω^m r}···d_r run over a full ω-orbit.

Base groupoid G:
- Objects: P^ω, Q_a, R_r.
- Arrows: a_r : R_r → R_{r'}, b_r : Q_a → R_r, c_a : P^ω → Q_a.

The extension G~ (top-right column of the page):
- Objects lie over the base objects: P~^ω_a over P^ω (one lift for each edge a of the face ω), Q~_a over Q_a, R~_r over R_r.
- The left column shows the functor G~ → G. The 'oblique' (horizontal) arrows a~_r, b~_r, c~^ω_a (= c~_r) map to a_r, b_r, c_a.
- The 'fibre' or 'vertical' arrows all map to 1. They are:
  - loops λ at each object P~, Q~, R~;
  - half-turns μ_{Q~_a} : Q~_a → Q~_a^∨ and μ_{R~_r} : R~_r → R~_r^∨ (the object with reversed orientation or order);
  - d~^ω_r : P~^ω_{a1} → P~^ω_a, joining successive lifts of the same face object.

Relations:
- (1) 'Hexagonal' relations: a~_r b~_r c~_r d~_r = b~_{r1} c~_{r2}. This is a lift of a cycle relation of the base groupoid, with the correction term d.
- (5) Going once around the ω-orbit gives the loop: d~_{ω^m r}···d~_r = λ_{P~^ω_{a1}}.
- (6), (7) Each half-turn squares to the loop: μ_{Q~^∨}μ_{Q~} = λ_{Q~} and μ_{R~^∨}μ_{R~} = λ_{R~}.
- (8)–(10) 'Transport' or 'commutation' relations: the oblique arrows carry λ to λ. So the loops form a central, transported Z.

Interpretation: the fibres of G~ → G are fundamental groupoids of circles with marked points. Over P^ω the fibre is a circle with one point per side of the face; over Q and R it is a circle with two antipodal points (an object and its 'dual'). G~ is thus a Z-central extension of G, a 'circle-bundle' groupoid. This is the familiar mechanism for passing from a groupoid built from a map or cell structure to its version with tangential base points, i.e. framed boundaries. In that version the Dehn twist λ is central, rotations around a face multiply to λ, and the braiding (half-twist) μ squares to λ.

This is the shape of the presentations of the 'extended' Teichmüller groupoid or Lego–Teichmüller game in genus 0, with:
- rotation Z with Z^n equal to the twist;
- braiding B with B^2 equal to the twist;
- hexagon relations;
- centrality of the twists.

The page is a bookkeeping table of generators and relations within the cote 'Groupoïdes de Teichmüller'. The neighbouring pages are blank or unrelated, so the exact base groupoid (which cells P, Q, R represent) is not determinable from this page alone.
errors: The objects Q~_a^∨ and R~_r^∨ appear as targets of μ but are not listed among the objects in the top-right column; presumably they are identified with other lifts or implicitly added. This is a gap in the bookkeeping.

Relation (1) mixes r, r1, r2 indices whose definitions are only partially written (r2 is not defined on the page). Relation (5) contains a crossed-out first attempt. The presentation is a working draft, not a checked one.
Relations (2)–(4) are missing from the numbering (the page jumps from ① to ⑤).

ideas.what: Central Z-extension of a combinatorially defined groupoid: lifting objects to several points over each base object, with vertical arrows being loops and half-loops (fibres are fundamental groupoids of marked circles)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid with tangential base points / framed (extended) Teichmüller groupoid as a central extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, tangential base points); developed explicitly by Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Funar–Gelca
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and base points at infinity, but not this explicit table

ideas.what: Half-twist μ with μ^∨μ = λ (braiding squares to the boundary Dehn twist)
ideas.modern_name: Braiding move B with B^2 = twist in the Moore–Seiberg / Lego–Teichmüller presentation

ideas.what: Product of the d-rotations around a face equals the loop λ
ideas.modern_name: Rotation move Z with Z^n = Dehn twist (balancing / ribbon relation)

ideas.what: Indexing generators by flags of a map, with σ0, σ1 cartographic operators and R ≃ A×ω ≃ S×ω
ideas.modern_name: Cartographic group / dessins combinatorics applied to groupoid presentations

missed.claim: An explicit generator-and-relation presentation of a Z-central 'tangential base point' extension of a groupoid indexed by the flags of a map. It includes oblique/vertical arrow types, twist-centrality ('transport') relations, half-twist-squared relations and rotation-cycle relations. This anticipates the shape of the later extended Teichmüller groupoid presentations (Bakalov–Kirillov, Funar–Gelca), here phrased via the cartographic flag set R with σ0, σ1.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck was working out the framed/central-extension version of his Teichmüller groupoid presentations in map-combinatorial terms. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft bookkeeping table of a central extension (twists, half-twists, rotations) of a map-indexed groupoid. It is consistent with, and predates, the published extended-Teichmüller presentations, but its content is now standard and the page is too fragmentary to show a distinct unpublished result.
transcription_corrections: The annotations 'renverser l'ordre' / 'renv. l'ordre', attached to curved arrows (λ_P ↔ λ_R, P~ ↔ R~ in the top-right column, and near μ), are editorial instructions to reverse the order of the list entries. They are not mathematical properties of Q_a or μ.
The left column should be recorded as the projection functor: a_r ← a~_r, b_r ← b~_r, c_a ← c~^ω_a, and 1 ← each vertical arrow (λ, μ, d). The vertical arrows map to identities.
In the top-right column the arrows go P^ω ← P~^ω_a, Q_a ← Q~_a, R_r ← R~_r (objects of the extension over base objects).
The label written as 'relations hexagonales' is hard to read in the image (it resembles 'relations h...ti...'); 'hexagonales' is a plausible but uncertain reading.
In (1), the right-hand side subscripts read b~_{r1} c~_{r2}; the image is consistent with this but r2 is undefined on the page.
In (6), the first factor is written μ_{Q~^∨_a} over a crossed-out subscript, prefixed by a correction mark '(5)α'.
